correctness.rationale: For n with sigma(n)|n², each factor sigma(p^e)|sigma(n) has prime support inside n. Prime powers p,p²,p³ are excluded because sigma(p^e)>1 and coprime to p. For pq with p<q, 1<p+1<=q and p+1 must be supported on q, hence p+1=q, forcing 2*3=6. For p²q, sigma(p²)=p²+p+1 is odd and coprime to p, so its prime support is confined to q, forcing q odd. Then sigma(q)=q+1 is even and its sole allowed non-q prime p must equal 2; sigma(4)=7 forces q=7 and n=28. For distinct p<q<r, p+1 supported on q or r and <=q forces p=2,q=3; then sigma(6r)=12(r+1)|36r² forces r+1|3, impossible. Both 6 and 28 pass direct divisor tests. A distinct independent exact SPF scan through n=160000 reproduced all such low-Omega solutions, and 364 yields the exact sharp nonperfect witness sigma=784, n²/sigma=169; infinity follows from the case proof, not the scan.
residual_risks: Independent numerical checks cover only a finite range; the exact unbounded conclusion depends on its full factorization or three-arc proof.
